extraction.name: VAP-Data
extraction.description: VAP-Data is the largest dataset for semantic-controlled video generation, containing over 100K curated paired videos across 100 semantic conditions. It covers 4 primary categories: concept (entity transformation and interaction), style, motion (human and non-human), and camera movement. The dataset was constructed to support unified semantic-controlled video generation research, enabling a single model to handle diverse semantic controls and generalize in a zero-shot manner to unseen semantics.
extraction.license: Research-only license with an acceptable-use policy (AUP) that explicitly prohibits abusive or unlawful scenarios
extraction.creator: Yuxuan Bian, Xin Chen, Zenan Li, Tiancheng Zhi, Shen Sang, Linjie Luo, Qiang Xu (Intelligent Creation Lab, ByteDance and The Chinese University of Hong Kong)
extraction.citeAs: Bian et al., Video-As-Prompt: Unified Semantic Control for Video Generation, arXiv:2510.20888v1 [cs.CV], October 23, 2025
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was constructed by curating approximately 2K high-quality real images from the Internet, spanning men, women, children, animals, objects, landscapes, and multi-subject cases. These images were then matched with Image-to-Video visual-effects templates from commercial models (VIDU and Kling) and community LoRAs to create paired videos by matching each image to all compatible templates. This bootstrapping approach was used because filming 100K real-world pairs is nearly impossible for research exploration.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Approximately 2K high-quality real images collected from the Internet, spanning men, women, children, animals, objects, landscapes, and multi-subject cases. Paired videos were generated using Image-to-Video visual-effects templates from commercial models (VIDU and Kling) and community LoRAs.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Each curated reference image was matched to all compatible visual-effects templates (some templates restrict subject categories). Commercial model APIs (VIDU, Kling) and community LoRAs were used as an automated engine to generate paired videos for each image-template combination, resulting in over 100K paired video samples across 100 semantic conditions.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Reference images were curated for quality and diversity. Each image was matched to compatible templates based on subject category restrictions. For evaluation, 24 semantic conditions were evenly sampled from 4 categories (concept, style, motion, camera) in the test subset, with 2 samples each, totaling 48 test samples.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Semantic alignment scoring was performed by submitting each (reference, generation) video pair along with detailed evaluation rules to Gemini-2.5-Pro for automatic scoring. The evaluation rules pair a general template with key criteria for each semantic condition. Semantic conditions were defined based on commercial model API definitions (Kling, Vidu) and community visual effects LoRA definitions. A user study with 20 randomly selected video-generation researchers was also conducted to evaluate video quality and semantic alignment via pairwise preference comparisons.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Gemini-2.5-Pro (automatic semantic alignment scoring); GPT-5 (validation of semantic alignment metric); human user study with 20 video-generation researchers
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The semantic alignment score evaluated by Gemini-2.5-Pro was validated against GPT-5 scores, which matched closely and followed the trends of human preference rates in the user study, confirming the validity of the metric. The user study reported preference rates as the normalized share of selections across all comparisons, totaling 100%.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: 20 randomly selected video-generation researchers participated in the user study.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Gemini-2.5-Pro (automatic semantic alignment scoring), GPT-5 (validation scoring), CLIP (text alignment metric), RAFT optical flow (dynamic degree metric), LAION aesthetic predictor (aesthetic quality metric)
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset will be released with a research-only license and an acceptable-use policy (AUP). No specific versioning, update schedule, or deprecation policy is described beyond the initial release.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset includes reference images and videos of men, women, and children, as well as semantic conditions involving gender swap, human motion transfer, and human identity-related transformations (e.g., gender swap, pet to human, sexy me, selfie with younger self).
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: VAP targets semantic-controlled video generation for research, education, and creative prototyping. Potential misuses include identity impersonation, deepfake content, targeted harassment, deceptive political messaging, and generation of sexualized or violent media. Mitigations include a research-only release and default content filters blocking clearly harmful categories (e.g., sexual content, explicit violence, hate symbols). The model is not intended for surveillance, impersonation, political persuasion, or other high-risk deployments.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: VAP-Data is synthetic and derived from other generative models (commercial APIs and community LoRAs), and may inherit the specific stylistic biases, artifacts, and conceptual limitations of the source templates. For example, if the source models are poor at generating hands, VAP will likely not learn to generate hands well from this data. The semantic conditions are relatively limited and synthetic compared to real-world diversity.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is synthetic and derived from generative models, which may introduce stylistic biases and artifacts from source templates. The semantic conditions covered are relatively limited. Building a large, real-world, semantic-controlled video dataset is identified as future work. Performance depends on caption quality and structural similarity between subjects; mismatched captions or large subject differences degrade generation quality. Multi-reference prompting can cause unwanted blending of visual details across videos.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training and evaluation of unified semantic-controlled video generation models. The dataset supports training a single generalist model to learn unified semantic control across diverse conditions (concept, style, motion, camera). It is intended for research, education, and creative prototyping. Not intended for surveillance, impersonation, political persuasion, or other high-risk deployments.
